def-diminishing-adaptation:
## Definition

Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ and $(\Gamma,\mathcal G)$ be nonempty measurable
spaces ([[def-measurable-space]]). Let $\pi$ be a probability measure on
$(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$, and let $(P_\gamma)_{\gamma\in\Gamma}$ be a jointly
measurable family of probability kernels on $\mathsf X$: for every
$A\in\mathcal X$, $(\gamma,x)\mapsto P_\gamma(x,A)$ is
$\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal X$-measurable and each $P_\gamma$ is a probability
kernel ([[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]). Assume that $\pi$ is
invariant for every fixed kernel, meaning $\pi P_\gamma=\pi$
([[def-invariant-and-stationary-distribution-for-a-markov-kernel]]).

An **adaptive MCMC process** is a pair of measurable processes
$(X_n,\Gamma_n)_{n\ge0}$ with $X_n\in\mathsf X$, $\Gamma_n\in\Gamma$, and
natural filtration $\mathcal F_n=\sigma(X_0,\Gamma_0,\ldots,X_n,\Gamma_n)$,
such that for every $A\in\mathcal X$,
$$\mathbb P(X_{n+1}\in A\mid\mathcal F_n)=P_{\Gamma_n}(X_n,A)\quad\text{a.s.}$$
The update rule for $\Gamma_{n+1}$ may depend on the history through time
$n+1$; it is required only to make $\Gamma_{n+1}$ a measurable random variable.

For $n\ge0$, define the adaptation size
$$D_n:=\sup_{x\in\mathsf X}\lVert P_{\Gamma_{n+1}}(x,\cdot)-P_{\Gamma_n}(x,\cdot)\rVert_{\rm TV},$$
where total variation uses the convention
$\lVert\mu-\nu\rVert_{\rm TV}=\sup_{A\in\mathcal X}|\mu(A)-\nu(A)|$
([[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]). Assume each $D_n$
is measurable; it lies in $[0,1]$. The process has **diminishing
adaptation** if $D_n\to0$ in probability as $n\to\infty$. This condition does
not require $\Gamma_n$ to converge.
lem-total-variation-coupling-and-kernel-:
## Statement

Let $\mu,\nu$ be probability measures on $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ and let
$P$ be a probability kernel on that space. Then
$$\lVert\mu-\nu\rVert_{\rm TV}=\sup_{f:\mathsf X\to[0,1]\ \mathcal X\text{-measurable}}\left|\int f\,d\mu-\int f\,d\nu\right|,$$
$$\lVert\mu P-\nu P\rVert_{\rm TV}\le\lVert\mu-\nu\rVert_{\rm TV}.$$
If $(U,V)$ is a coupling of $\mu$ and $\nu$ on a probability space and
$E$ is a measurable event on which $U=V$, then
$$\lVert\mu-\nu\rVert_{\rm TV}\le\mathbb P(E^c).$$
def-adaptive-mcmc-containment:
## Definition

Use the adaptive MCMC setup of [[def-diminishing-adaptation]]. For
$\epsilon>0$, a state $x\in\mathsf X$, and a fixed parameter $\gamma\in\Gamma$,
define the convergence time
$$M_\epsilon(x,\gamma):=\inf\{m\in\mathbb N:m\ge1,\ \lVert P_\gamma^m(x,\cdot)-\pi\rVert_{\rm TV}\le\epsilon\},$$
with $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$. The power $P_\gamma^m$ is the $m$-fold
composition of the fixed kernel $P_\gamma$; it is not the adaptive transition
law. Assume $M_\epsilon(X_n,\Gamma_n)$ is measurable for each $n$ and
$\epsilon>0$.

For a specified initial probability law $\mu_0$ of $(X_0,\Gamma_0)$, the
adaptive process has **containment** if for every $\epsilon,\delta>0$ there is
an integer $N=N(\epsilon,\delta)$ such that
$$\mathbb P_{\mu_0}\!\left(M_\epsilon(X_n,\Gamma_n)\le N\right)\ge1-\delta\quad\text{for every }n\ge0.$$
A fixed initial pair $(x_*,\gamma_*)$ is the special case
$\mu_0=\delta_{(x_*,\gamma_*)}$, equivalently the same probability bound
conditional on $X_0=x_*$ and $\Gamma_0=\gamma_*$. Thus containment says that
the fixed-kernel convergence times, evaluated at the current state and
parameter, form a sequence bounded in probability under the specified initial
law. It does not assert a uniform deterministic bound for every possible
state and parameter.
lem-adaptive-mcmc-block-perturbation-bou:
## Statement

Let $(X_n,\Gamma_n)$ be an adaptive MCMC process with adaptation sizes $D_n$
as in [[def-diminishing-adaptation]]. For integers $n\ge0$ and $N\ge1$, define
the frozen-kernel mixture $Q_{n,N}$ by
$$Q_{n,N}(A):=\mathbb E\!\left[P_{\Gamma_n}^{N}(X_n,A)\right]\quad(A\in\mathcal X).$$
Then $Q_{n,N}$ is a probability measure and
$$\left\lVert\mathcal L(X_{n+N})-Q_{n,N}\right\rVert_{\rm TV}\le\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\sum_{j=0}^{i-1}\mathbb E[D_{n+j}],$$
where the inner sum is $0$ for $i=0$.
lem-adaptive-mcmc-uniform-drift-minoriza:
## Statement

Let $(P_\gamma)_{\gamma\in\Gamma}$ be probability kernels on a measurable
space $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ with a common invariant probability $\pi$
([[def-invariant-and-stationary-distribution-for-a-markov-kernel]]). Suppose
there are a measurable set $C$, a finite measurable $V:\mathsf X\to[1,\infty)$,
and constants $v\ge1$, $0<\delta\le1$, $0<\lambda<1$, and $0\le b<\infty$
such that $\sup_{x\in C}V(x)\le v$ and, for every $\gamma$, there is a
probability measure $\nu_\gamma$ with $\nu_\gamma(C)=1$ satisfying
$$P_\gamma(x,A)\ge\delta\nu_\gamma(A)\quad(x\in C,\ A\in\mathcal X),\qquad P_\gamma V(x):=\int V(y)P_\gamma(x,dy)\le\lambda V(x)+b1_C(x)\quad(x\in\mathsf X).$$
Then there are constants $M<\infty$ and $0<\rho<1$, depending only on
$v,\delta,\lambda,b$, such that
$$\lVert P_\gamma^n(x,\cdot)-\pi\rVert_{\rm TV}\le M V(x)\rho^n\quad(x\in\mathsf X,\ n\ge0,\ \gamma\in\Gamma).$$
The support condition $\nu_\gamma(C)=1$ is the strong-aperiodicity
hypothesis in the cited drift/minorization route.
thm-adaptive-mcmc-converges-under-unifor:
## Statement

Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ and $(\Gamma,\mathcal G)$, the jointly
measurable probability-kernel family $(P_\gamma)_{\gamma\in\Gamma}$, common
invariant probability $\pi$, and adaptive process $(X_n,\Gamma_n)$ satisfy
[[def-diminishing-adaptation]]. Fix an initial law $\mu_0$ for
$(X_0,\Gamma_0)$; a fixed initial pair is the Dirac-law special case. If
diminishing adaptation holds under this law and either of the following
conditions holds, then
$$\lVert\mathcal L_{\mu_0}(X_n)-\pi\rVert_{\rm TV}\longrightarrow0.$$

1. **Simultaneous uniform ergodicity:** for every $\epsilon>0$ there is an
   integer $N(\epsilon)\ge1$ such that
   $$\sup_{x\in\mathsf X,\,\gamma\in\Gamma}\lVert P_\gamma^{N(\epsilon)}(x,\cdot)-\pi\rVert_{\rm TV}\le\epsilon.$$

2. **Containment:** for every $\epsilon,\delta>0$ there is an integer $N$
   such that
   $$\mathbb P_{\mu_0}\!\left(M_\epsilon(X_n,\Gamma_n)\le N\right)\ge1-\delta\quad\text{for every }n\ge0,$$
   where $M_\epsilon$ is the fixed-kernel convergence time from
   [[def-adaptive-mcmc-containment]].

The conclusion is convergence of the one-time marginal distributions. It does
not itself assert a strong law, a central limit theorem, or convergence of
sample averages.
cor-adaptive-mcmc-containment-from-unifo:
## Statement

Assume the adaptive MCMC setup and diminishing adaptation of
[[def-diminishing-adaptation]]. Suppose the common target, set $C$, drift
function $V$, and constants satisfy the hypotheses of
[[lem-adaptive-mcmc-uniform-drift-minorization-bound]], including the
strong-aperiodicity condition $\nu_\gamma(C)=1$ for every $\gamma$. If
$\mathbb E[V(X_0)]<\infty$, then containment holds for the initial law of
$(X_0,\Gamma_0)$, and the marginal laws converge to $\pi$ in total variation.
